text:
Let $\mathrm{L}_{1}:\frac{x-1}{1}=\frac{y-2}{-1}=\frac{z-1}{2}$ and $\mathrm{L}_{2}:\frac{x+1}{-1}=\frac{y-2}{2}=\frac{z}{1}$ be two lines.

Let $L_{3}$ be a line passing through the point $(α,β,γ)$ and be perpendicular to both $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$. If $L_{3}$ intersects $\mathrm{L}_{1}$, then $|5α-11β-8γ|$ equals :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Step 1. Identify the Given Lines

The line 

$\mathrm{L}_{1}:\frac{x-1}{1}=\frac{y-2}{-1}=\frac{z-1}{2}$ 

passes through the point 

$P_{1}=(1,2,1)$ 

with direction vector 

$𝐮=(1,-1,2).$

Similarly, the line 

$\mathrm{L}_{2}:\frac{x+1}{-1}=\frac{y-2}{2}=\frac{z}{1}$ 

passes through the point 

$P_{2}=(-1,2,0)$ 

with direction vector 

$𝐯=(-1,2,1).$

Step 2. Determine the Direction of $L_{3}$

Since $L_{3}$ is perpendicular to both $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$, its direction vector must be parallel to the cross product of $𝐮$ and $𝐯$. Compute:

$𝐝=𝐮\times 𝐯=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 𝐢 & 𝐣 & 𝐤 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 \end{array}\right |.$

Using the determinant, we obtain:

$\begin{array}{ll} d_{x} & =(-1)(1)-(2)(2)=-1-4=-5, \\ d_{y} & =(2)(-1)-(1)(1)=-2-1=-3, \\ d_{z} & =(1)(2)-(-1)(-1)=2-1=1. \end{array}$

Thus, a valid direction vector is 

$𝐝=(-5,-3,1).$

Step 3. Express $L_{3}$ in Terms of Its Intersection with $L_{1}$

Since $L_{3}$ intersects $L_{1}$, let the intersection point (on $L_{1}$) be expressed using a parameter $t$ as:

$A(t)=(1+t,2-t,1+2t).$

Since $L_{3}$ passes through $A(t)$ and also through the given point 

$Q=(α,β,γ),$ 

its parametric form can be written as:

$(α,β,γ)=A(t)+s𝐝=(1+t,2-t,1+2t)+s(-5,-3,1)$

for some parameters $s$ and $t$.

Step 4. Express $α,β,γ$ in Terms of $t$ and $s$

Comparing coordinates, we have:

$\left \{\begin{array}{l} α=1+t-5s, \\ β=2-t-3s, \\ γ=1+2t+s. \end{array} \right.$

Step 5. Compute $5α-11β-8γ$

Substitute the expressions for $α$, $β$, and $γ$:

$\begin{array}{ll} 5α-11β-8γ & =5(1+t-5s)-11(2-t-3s)-8(1+2t+s) \\ =(5+5t-25s)-(22-11t-33s)-(8+16t+8s) \\ =(5-22-8)+(5t+11t-16t)+(-25s+33s-8s) \\ =-25+0t+0s \\ =-25. \end{array}$

Taking the absolute value yields:

$|5α-11β-8γ|=25.$

Conclusion

The value of 

$|5α-11β-8γ|$ is $25.$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: Let $P$ be the set of seven digit numbers with sum of their digits equal to 11. If the numbers in $P$ are formed by using the digits 1, 2 and 3 only, then the number of elements in the set $P$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the number contain $a$ ones, $b$ twos and $c$ threes. Then $a+b+c=7$ and $a+2b+3c=11$; subtracting, $b+2c=4$.

The non-negative solutions are $(b,c)=(4,0),(2,1),(0,2)$, giving $a=3,4,5$ respectively.

Digits $1,1,1,2,2,2,2$: $\dfrac{7!}{3!4!}=35$ numbers.

Digits $1,1,1,1,2,2,3$: $\dfrac{7!}{4!2!1!}=105$ numbers.

Digits $1,1,1,1,1,3,3$: $\dfrac{7!}{5!2!}=21$ numbers.

$n(P)=35+105+21=161$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: Let $A=[\begin{array}{l} a_{ij} \end{array}]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \log _{5}128 & \log _{4}5 \\ \log _{5}8 & \log _{4}25 \end{array}\right ]$. If $A_{ij}$ is the cofactor of $a_{ij}$, $C_{ij}=\sum\limits _{k=1}^{2}a_{ik}A_{jk},1\leq i,j\leq 2$, and $C=[C_{ij}]$, then $8|C|$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The $(k,j)$ entry of $\mathrm{adj}A$ is $A_{jk}$, so $C_{ij}=\sum\limits _{k=1}^{2}a_{ik}A_{jk}$ is the $(i,j)$ entry of $A(\mathrm{adj}A)$. Hence $C=A(\mathrm{adj}A)=|A|I_{2}$ and $|C|=|A|^{2}$.

Using $\log _{4}25=\log _{2}5$, $\log _{4}5=\dfrac{1}{2}\log _{2}5$, $\log _{5}128=7\log _{5}2$, $\log _{5}8=3\log _{5}2$ and $\log _{2}5\cdot \log _{5}2=1$:

$|A|=(7\log _{5}2)(\log _{2}5)-\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\log _{2}5\right )(3\log _{5}2)=7-\dfrac{3}{2}=\dfrac{11}{2}.$

$8|C|=8|A|^{2}=8\times \dfrac{121}{4}=242.$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: Consider an A. P. of positive integers, whose sum of the first three terms is 54 and the sum of the first twenty terms lies between 1600 and 1800. Then its $11^{th}$ term is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the first term be $a$ and the common difference $d$; both are integers since every term is a positive integer.

$S_{3}=3a+3d=54\Rightarrow a+d=18\Rightarrow 2a=36-2d$.

$S_{20}=\dfrac{20}{2}(2a+19d)=10(36-2d+19d)=10(36+17d)$.

$1600<10(36+17d)<1800\Rightarrow 160<36+17d<180\Rightarrow 124<17d<144\Rightarrow 7\frac{5}{17}<d<8\frac{8}{17}$.

The only integer value is $d=8$, so $a=18-8=10$ (then $S_{20}=10\times 172=1720$).

$a_{11}=a+10d=10+80=90$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: Two parabolas have the same focus (4, 3) and their directrices are the x-axis and the y-axis, respectively. If these parabolas intersect at the points A and B, then $(AB)^{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A point $(x,y)$ of a parabola is equidistant from the focus $(4,3)$ and the directrix.

Directrix the $x$-axis (distance $|y|$):

$(x-4)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}=y^{2}$

Directrix the $y$-axis (distance $|x|$):

$(x-4)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}=x^{2}$

At an intersection point the right sides are equal, so $x^{2}=y^{2}$, i.e. $y=x$ or $y=-x$.

With $y=-x$: $(x-4)^{2}+(x+3)^{2}=x^{2}\Rightarrow x^{2}-2x+25=0$, whose discriminant $4-100<0$, so there is no real point.

With $y=x$: $(x-4)^{2}+(x-3)^{2}=x^{2}\Rightarrow x^{2}-14x+25=0$. Its roots $x_{1},x_{2}$ give $A(x_{1},x_{1})$ and $B(x_{2},x_{2})$, with $x_{1}+x_{2}=14$ and $x_{1}x_{2}=25$.

$AB^{2}=2(x_{1}-x_{2})^{2}=2\left [(x_{1}+x_{2})^{2}-4x_{1}x_{2}\right ]=2(196-100)=192$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: The least value of n for which the number of integral terms in the Binomial expansion of $(\sqrt{3 7}+\sqrt{12 11})^{n}$ is 183, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The general term is $T_{r+1}={}^{n}C_{r}7^{\frac{n-r}{3}}11^{\frac{r}{12}}$, $r=0,1,\ldots ,n$.

It is an integer when $12|r$ and $3|(n-r)$. Since $12|r$ already gives $3|r$, the second condition becomes $3|n$.

With $3|n$, the admissible values are $r=12k$ for $k=0,1,2,\ldots ,⌊\dfrac{n}{12}⌋$, so the number of integral terms is $⌊\dfrac{n}{12}⌋+1$.

$⌊\dfrac{n}{12}⌋+1=183\Rightarrow ⌊\dfrac{n}{12}⌋=182\Rightarrow 2184\leq n\leq 2195$

The least such $n$ is $2184=12\times 182$, which is a multiple of $3$. For $n=2196$, $r=0,12,\ldots ,2196$ gives $184$ integral terms.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: The value of $\lim _{n\to \infty }\left (\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}\frac{k^{3}+6k^{2}+11k+5}{(k+3)!}\right )$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \lim _{n\to \infty }\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}\dfrac{k^{3}+6k^{2}+11k+5}{(k+3)!} \\ =\lim _{n\to \infty }\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}\dfrac{k^{3}+6k^{2}+11k+6-1}{(k+3)!} \\ =\lim _{n\to \infty }\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}\dfrac{(k+1)(k+2)(k+3)-1}{(k+3)!} \\ =\lim _{n\to \infty }\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}\dfrac{(k+1)(k+2)(k+3)}{(k+3)!}-\dfrac{1}{(k+3)!} \\ =\lim _{n\to \infty }\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}\left (\dfrac{1}{k!}-\dfrac{1}{(k+3)!}\right ) \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} =\lim _{\mathrm{n}\to \infty }\left (\dfrac{1}{1!}+\dfrac{1}{2!}+\dfrac{1}{3!}+\dfrac{1}{4!}\ldots +\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{n}!}-\dfrac{1}{4!}-\dfrac{1}{5!}-\dfrac{1}{6!}\ldots -\dfrac{1}{(\mathrm{n}+3)!}\right ) \\ =\dfrac{1}{1}+\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{1}{6}=\dfrac{10}{6}=\dfrac{5}{3} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text:
Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation :

$\cos x(\log _{e}(\cos x))^{2}dy+(\sin x-3y\sin x\log _{e}(\cos x))dx=0$, x ∈ (0, $\frac{π}{2}$ ). If $y(\frac{π}{4})$ = $-\frac{1}{\log _{e}2}$, then $y(\frac{π}{6})$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \cos x(\ln (\cos x))^{2}dy+(\sin x-3y(\sin x)\ln (\cos x))dx=0 \\ \cos x(\ln (\cos x))^{2}\dfrac{dy}{dx}-3\sin x\cdot \ln (\cos x)y=-\sin x \\ \dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{3\tan x}{\ln (\cos x)}y=\dfrac{-\tan x}{(\ln (\cos x))^{2}} \\ \dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{3\tan x}{\ln (\sec x)}y=\dfrac{-\tan x}{(\ln (\sec x))^{2}} \\ \text{I.F.}=e^{\int \frac{3\tan x}{\ln (\sec x)}dx}=(\ln (\sec x))^{3} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} y\times (\ln (\sec x))^{3}=-\int \dfrac{\tan x}{(\ln (\sec x))^{2}}(\ln (\sec x))^{3}dx \\ y\times (\ln (\sec x))^{3}=-\dfrac{1}{2}(\ln (\sec x))^{2}+C \\ \text{Given}:x=\dfrac{π}{4},y=-\dfrac{1}{\ln 2} \\ \dfrac{-1}{\ln 2}\times (\ln \sqrt{2})^{3}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\times (\ln \sqrt{2})^{2}+C \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{-1}{8\ln 2}\times (\ln 2)^{3}=\dfrac{-1}{2}\times \dfrac{1}{4}(\ln 2)^{2}+C \\ -\dfrac{1}{8}(\ln 2)^{2}=\dfrac{-1}{8}(\ln 2)^{2}+C \\ \Rightarrow C=0 \\ \therefore y(\ln (\sec x))^{3}=\dfrac{-1}{2}(\ln (\sec x))^{2}+0 \\ y=\dfrac{-1}{2\ln (\sec x)} \\ y=\dfrac{1}{2\ln (\cos x)} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore y\left (\dfrac{π}{6}\right )=\dfrac{1}{2\ln \left (\cos \frac{π}{6}\right )} \\ =\dfrac{1}{2\ln \left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )} \\ =\dfrac{1}{2\left (\frac{1}{2}\ln 3-\ln 2\right )} \\ =\dfrac{1}{\ln 3-\ln 4} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: Let $x_{1},x_{2},...,x_{10}$ be ten observations such that $\sum\limits _{i=1}^{10}(x_{i}-2)=30$, $\sum\limits _{i=1}^{10}(x_{i}-β)^{2}=98$, $β>2$, and their variance is $\frac{4}{5}$. If $μ$ and $σ^{2}$ are respectively the mean and the variance of $2(x_{1}-1)+4β,2(x_{2}-1)+4β,...,2(x_{10}-1)+4β$, then $\frac{βμ}{σ^{2}}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $\sum\limits _{i=1}^{10}(x_{i}-2)=30$, so $\sum x_{i}-20=30\Rightarrow \sum x_{i}=50$ and the mean of the $x_{i}$ is $5$.

From the variance, $\dfrac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{10}-5^{2}=\dfrac{4}{5}\Rightarrow \sum x_{i}^{2}=10\left (25+\dfrac{4}{5}\right )=258$.

Expanding the second condition:

$\sum\limits _{i=1}^{10}(x_{i}-β)^{2}=\sum x_{i}^{2}-2β\sum x_{i}+10β^{2}=258-100β+10β^{2}=98$

$\Rightarrow β^{2}-10β+16=0\Rightarrow (β-8)(β-2)=0$, and $β>2$ gives $β=8$.

The new observations are $2(x_{i}-1)+4β=2x_{i}+30$.

Their mean is $μ=2(5)+30=40$. Adding a constant leaves the variance unchanged and multiplying by $2$ multiplies it by $4$, so $σ^{2}=4\times \dfrac{4}{5}=\dfrac{16}{5}$.

$\frac{βμ}{σ^{2}}=\frac{8\times 40}{16/5}=\frac{320\times 5}{16}=100$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

using equation (1)

text: Let the line $x+y=1$ meet the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=4$ at the points A and B. If the line perpendicular to AB and passing through the mid-point of the chord AB intersects the circle at C and D, then the area of the quadrilateral ABCD is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The perpendicular bisector of a chord passes through the centre, so the line through the mid-point of AB perpendicular to $x+y=1$ is $y=x$, and CD is the diameter of $x^{2}+y^{2}=4$ along it:

$CD=4$

The distance of the centre $O(0,0)$ from $x+y=1$ is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, so

$AB=2\sqrt{4-\dfrac{1}{2}}=2\sqrt{\dfrac{7}{2}}=\sqrt{14}$


[IMG]

On the circle the points occur in the order A, C, B, D, so AB and CD are the diagonals of the quadrilateral, and they are perpendicular. The area is therefore

$\dfrac{1}{2}\times AB\times CD=\dfrac{1}{2}\times \sqrt{14}\times 4=2\sqrt{14}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: Define a relation R on the interval $\left [0,\frac{π}{2}\right )$ by $x$ R $y$ if and only if $\sec ^{2}x-\tan ^{2}y=1$. Then R is :
options: both reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
both reflexive and transitive but not symmetric
reflexive but neither symmetric nor transitive
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \sec ^{2}x-\tan ^{2}x=1(\text{on replacing}y\text{with}x) \\ \Rightarrow \text{Reflexive} \\ \sec ^{2}x-\tan ^{2}y=1 \\ \Rightarrow 1+\tan ^{2}x+1-\sec ^{2}y=1 \\ \Rightarrow \sec ^{2}y-\tan ^{2}x=1 \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{symmetric} \\ \sec ^{2}x-\tan ^{2}y=1 \\ \sec ^{2}y-\tan ^{2}z=1 \end{array}$

Adding both

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \sec ^{2}x-\tan ^{2}y+\sec ^{2}y-\tan ^{2}z=1+1 \\ \sec ^{2}x+1-\tan ^{2}z=2 \\ \sec ^{2}x-\tan ^{2}z=1 \\ \Rightarrow \text{Transitive} \end{array}$

hence equivalence relation

text:
Let M and m respectively be the maximum and the minimum values of

$f(x)=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1+\sin ^{2}x & \cos ^{2}x & 4\sin 4x \\ \sin ^{2}x & 1+\cos ^{2}x & 4\sin 4x \\ \sin ^{2}x & \cos ^{2}x & 1+4\sin 4x \end{array}\right |,x\in R$

Then $M^{4}-m^{4}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{lllllll} \left |\begin{array}{lll} 1+\sin ^{2}x & \cos ^{2}x & 4\sin 4x \\ \sin ^{2}x & 1+\cos ^{2}x & 4\sin 4x \\ \sin ^{2}x & \cos ^{2}x & 1+4\sin 4x \end{array}\right |,x\in R \\ R_{2}\to R_{2}-R_{1}&R_{3}\to R_{3}-R_{1} \\ f(x)=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1+\sin ^{2}x & \cos ^{2}x & 4\sin 4x \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right | \end{array}$

Expand about $\mathrm{R}_{1}$, we get

$f(x)=2+4\sin 4x$

$\therefore M=\max$ value of $f(x)=6$

$\mathrm{m}=\min$ value of $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=-2$

$\therefore \mathrm{M}^{4}-\mathrm{m}^{4}=1280$

text: The integral $80\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}\left (\frac{\sin θ+\cos θ}{9+16\sin 2θ}\right )dθ$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} I=80\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}\left (\dfrac{\sin θ+\cos θ}{9+16(2\sin θ\cdot \cos θ)}\right )dθ \\ =80\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}\dfrac{\sin θ+\cos θ}{9-16(1-2\sin θ\cdot \cos θ-1)}dθ \end{array}$

$\left. \begin{array}{l} =80\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}\dfrac{\sin θ+\cos θ}{9+16-16(\sin θ-\cos θ)^{2}}\mathrm{d}θ \\ \text{Let}\sin θ-\cos θ=\mathrm{t} \\ (\cos θ+\sin θ)\mathrm{d}θ=\mathrm{dt} \\ =80\int\limits _{-1}^{0}\dfrac{\mathrm{dt}}{25-16\mathrm{t}^{2}} \\ =\dfrac{80}{16}\int\limits _{-1}^{0}\dfrac{\mathrm{dt}}{\left (\frac{5}{4}\right )^{2}-\mathrm{t}^{2}} \\ =\dfrac{5}{2\left (\frac{5}{4}\right )}\ln \left |\dfrac{\frac{5}{4}+t}{\frac{5}{4}-t}\right |\right ]_{-1}^{0} \\ =2\ln (1)+4\ln 3 \\ =4\ln 3 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text:
Let [t] be the greatest integer less than or equal to t. Then the least value of p ∈ N for which

$\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}\left (x\left (\left [\frac{1}{x}\right ]+\left [\frac{2}{x}\right ]+\ldots +\left [\frac{p}{x}\right ]\right )-x^{2}\left (\left [\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right ]+\left [\frac{2^{2}}{x^{2}}\right ]+\ldots +\left [\frac{9^{2}}{x^{2}}\right ]\right )\right )\geq 1$ is equal to $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the least natural number $p$ for which the following inequality holds:

$\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}\left (x\left (\left [\frac{1}{x}\right ]+\left [\frac{2}{x}\right ]+\ldots +\left [\frac{p}{x}\right ]\right )-x^{2}\left (\left [\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right ]+\left [\frac{2^{2}}{x^{2}}\right ]+\ldots +\left [\frac{9^{2}}{x^{2}}\right ]\right )\right )\geq 1$

we simplify the expression inside the limit. 

As $x\to 0^{+}$, $\left [\frac{n}{x}\right ]$ approximates to $\frac{n}{x}$. Thus, the problem becomes finding:

$(1+2+\ldots +p)-\left (1^{2}+2^{2}+\ldots +9^{2}\right )\geq 1$

The sum of the first $p$ natural numbers is given by:

$\frac{p(p+1)}{2}$

And the sum of the squares of the first 9 natural numbers is:

$1^{2}+2^{2}+\ldots +9^{2}=\frac{9\cdot 10\cdot 19}{6}$

Thus, the inequality becomes:

$\frac{p(p+1)}{2}-\frac{9\cdot 10\cdot 19}{6}\geq 1$

Solving this, we rewrite:

$p(p+1)\geq 572$

The least natural number $p$ satisfying this condition is $24$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: Let $S=\left \{m\in 𝐙:A^{m^{2}}+A^{m}=3I-A^{-6}\right \}$, where $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ]$. Then $n(S)$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{lllllllllll} \begin{array}{lllllll} A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ] \\ A^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 3 & -2 \\ 2 & -1 \end{array}\right ],A^{3}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 4 & -3 \\ 3 & -2 \end{array}\right ],A^{4}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 5 & -4 \\ 4 & -3 \end{array}\right ] \end{array} \\ \text{and so on} \\ \begin{array}{lllll} \mathrm{A}^{6}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 7 & -6 \\ 6 & -5 \end{array}\right ] \\ \mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{m}}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{m}+1 & -\mathrm{m} \\ \mathrm{m} & -\mathrm{m}+1 \end{array}\right ], \\ \mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{m}^{2}}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{m}^{2}+1 & -\mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \mathrm{m}^{2} & -\left (\mathrm{m}^{2}-1\right ) \end{array}\right ] \\ \mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{m}^{2}}+\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{m}}=3\mathrm{I}-\mathrm{A}^{-6} \\ \left [\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{m}^{2}+1 & -\mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \mathrm{m}^{2} & -\left (\mathrm{m}^{2}-1\right ) \end{array}\right ]+\left [\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{m}+1 & -\mathrm{m} \\ \mathrm{m} & -\mathrm{m}+1 \end{array}\right ] \end{array} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{lllll} =3\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]-\left [\begin{array}{ll} -5 & 6 \\ -6 & 7 \end{array}\right ] \\ =\left [\begin{array}{ll} 8 & -6 \\ 6 & -4 \end{array}\right ] \\ =\mathrm{m}^{2}+1+\mathrm{m}+1=8 \\ =\mathrm{m}^{2}+\mathrm{m}-6=0\Rightarrow \mathrm{m}=-3,2 \\ \mathrm{n}(\mathrm{s})=2 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: Let S = $\left \{x:\cos ^{-1}x=π+\sin ^{-1}x+\sin ^{-1}(2x+1)\right \}$. Then $\sum\limits _{x\in S}(2x-1)^{2}$ is equal to $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \cos ^{-1}x=π+\sin ^{-1}x+\sin ^{-1}(2x+1) \\ 2\cos ^{-1}x-\sin ^{-1}(2x+1)=\dfrac{3π}{2} \\ 2α-β=\dfrac{3π}{2}\text{where}\cos ^{-1}x=α,\sin ^{-1}(2x+1)=β \\ 2α=\dfrac{3π}{2}+β \\ \cos 2α=\sin β \\ \begin{array}{l} 2\cos ^{2}α-1=\sin β \\ 2x^{2}-1=2x+1 \\ x^{2}-x-1=0 \\ \Rightarrow x=\frac{1-\sqrt{5}}{2},\left \{x=\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}\text{rejected}\right \} \\ \therefore 4x^{2}-4x=4 \\ (2x-1)^{2}=5 \end{array} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: Let $f:(0,\infty )\to 𝐑$ be a twice differentiable function. If for some $a\neq 0,\int\limits _{0}^{1}f(λx)\mathrm{d}λ=af(x),f(1)=1$ and $f(16)=\frac{1}{8}$, then $16-f^{'}\left (\frac{1}{16}\right )$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \int\limits _{0}^{1}\mathrm{f}(λ\mathrm{x})\mathrm{d}λ=\mathrm{af}(\mathrm{x}) \\ λ\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{t} \\ \mathrm{d}λ=\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{dt} \\ \dfrac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\int\limits _{0}^{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{t})\mathrm{dt}=\mathrm{af}(\mathrm{x}) \\ \int\limits _{0}^{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{t})\mathrm{dt}=\mathrm{axf}(\mathrm{x}) \\ \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{a}\left (\mathrm{x}\mathrm{f}^{'}(\mathrm{x})+\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})\right ) \\ (1-\mathrm{a})\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{a}\cdot \mathrm{x}\mathrm{f}^{'}(\mathrm{x}) \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{f}^{'}(\mathrm{x})}{\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})}=\dfrac{(1-\mathrm{a})}{\mathrm{a}}\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{x}} \\ \ln \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\dfrac{1-\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{a}}\ln \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{c} \\ \mathrm{x}=1,\mathrm{f}(1)=1\Rightarrow \mathrm{c}=0 \\ \mathrm{x}=16,\mathrm{f}(16)=\dfrac{1}{8} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{1}{8}=(16)^{\frac{1-a}{a}}\Rightarrow -3=\dfrac{4-4a}{a}\Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=4 \\ \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x}^{-\frac{3}{4}} \\ \mathrm{f}^{'}(\mathrm{x})=-\dfrac{3}{4}\mathrm{x}^{-\frac{7}{4}} \\ \therefore \quad 16-\mathrm{f}^{'}\left (\dfrac{1}{16}\right ) \\ =16-\left (-\dfrac{3}{4}\left (2^{-4}\right )^{-7/4}\right ) \\ =16+96=112 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: The number of 6-letter words, with or without meaning, that can be formed using the letters of the word MATHS such that any letter that appears in the word must appear at least twice, is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(i) Single letter is used, then no. of words $=5$

(ii) Two distinct letters are used, then no. of words

${}^{5}\mathrm{C}_{2}\times \left (\frac{6!}{2!4!}\times 2+\frac{6!}{3!3!}\right )=10(30+20)=500$

(iii) Three distinct letters are used, then no. of words

${}^{5}\mathrm{C}_{3}\times \frac{6!}{2!2!2!}=900$

Total no. of words $=1405$
